prodml-001.base: Is it data drift, label drift, or concept drift? How do you distinguish?
variants: Input feature distributions are unchanged, but the share of positive labels has doubled. Which kind of drift is that, and what does it imply for the model?
How would you work out whether the relationship between features and target has changed, rather than just the inputs?

prodml-001.base: You find the issue but fixing it requires retraining on all historical data (very expensive). What do you do?
variants: A full retrain costs $20,000 in compute and takes a week. What cheaper options do you try first?
Could you retrain on only recent data, or recalibrate the outputs instead? What are the risks of each?

prodml-002.base: What metrics do you monitor? Accuracy? Fairness? Prediction distribution? All of the above?
variants: The model's labels arrive 60 days late. What do you monitor in the meantime?
For a model that ranks search results, which health metrics matter, and how are they different from a credit model's?

prodml-002.base: You get 100 drift alerts per week. How do you avoid alert fatigue?
variants: Most drift alerts come from features with little effect on the model's predictions. How would you use that to cut noise?
How would you set drift thresholds so that an alert usually means something worth acting on?

prodml-002.base: Should you auto-retrain when drift is detected, or always get human approval?
variants: Automatic retraining kicked in after a data bug and the new model was worse. How should the process have been designed?
Which kinds of model would you let retrain automatically, and which always need a human sign-off?

prodml-003.base: Is this due to your features, or is the underlying data reflecting real but unfair patterns?
variants: Historical approval data reflects past lending decisions that disadvantaged a group. How does that end up in your model?
How would you tell whether a gap in approval rates comes from the model or from genuine differences in repayment?

prodml-003.base: You can't use 'protected attributes' as features, but the model is still making disparate predictions. How do you fix this?
variants: You removed gender as a feature, but approval rates still differ by gender. Which features might be acting as proxies, and how do you find them?
Zip code is highly predictive of default but also correlates with race. What do you do with it?

prodml-003.base: Removing the bias hurts model accuracy. How do you decide if the tradeoff is acceptable?
variants: The fairer model approves more applicants who later default, costing about $2M a year. Who decides whether that's acceptable, and how?
How would you present the fairness-accuracy trade-off to leadership so they can make a decision?

prodml-004.base: Do you do a canary deployment (small % of traffic), shadow mode (run both models), or full rollout?
variants: The forecast feeds a dashboard that finance uses once a month. Does a canary deployment make sense? What would you do instead?
When would shadow mode tell you nothing useful about the new model?

prodml-004.base: The new model is slightly less accurate overall but much better for certain segments. How do you evaluate this?
variants: The new model is 2% worse overall but 15% better for your largest customers. How do you decide?
How would you check whether a new model's improvement is concentrated in segments the business doesn't care about?

prodml-004.base: How long do you need to monitor before deciding the deployment was successful?
variants: The forecasts are monthly. How long do you run old and new side by side before deciding?
What would make you roll back after a week, even if overall accuracy looked fine?

prodml-005.base: How would you detect it after launch?
variants: Your model's online AUC is 0.70 but offline it was 0.82. What logs would you compare to check for skew?
How would you set up an automated check that serving-time features match what the training pipeline would compute?

prodml-005.base: Why do point-in-time correct joins matter when building training data?
variants: Your training set joins each loan to the customer's current income rather than income at application time. What does that do?
How would you build a training row so every feature reflects only what was known at prediction time?

prodml-005.base: Where does skew usually come from in practice?
variants: The data science team computes 'days since last login' in Python, and the engineering team reimplemented it in Java for serving. What can go wrong?
Which kinds of features are most prone to skew in your experience, and why?

prodml-006.base: Someone asks why last quarter's forecast said X. How would you answer?
variants: An auditor asks you to reproduce a prediction made eight months ago for a specific customer. What would you need to have saved?
Last quarter's forecast differs from what today's code produces for the same quarter. How do you find out why?

prodml-006.base: What can still make a run non-deterministic even with a fixed random seed?
variants: You fixed every seed, but training on a GPU gives slightly different results each run. Why?
Two runs with the same code and seed give different models on different machines. What could differ?

prodml-006.base: What would you version besides the code?
variants: Your code is in git. What else must be versioned so a training run can be repeated exactly?
How would you version a 500 GB training dataset without copying it each time?

prodml-007.base: How do you find where the time actually goes?
variants: Average latency is 80 ms but the 99th percentile is 900 ms. Where do you start looking?
How would you profile an inference service to see time spent on features, the model and network calls?

prodml-007.base: Which predictions could be precomputed instead of computed on request?
variants: Recommendations for most users only change once a day. What would you precompute, and what must stay online?
When does precomputing predictions for every user cost more than computing them on request?

prodml-007.base: How do you measure what you give up in accuracy for each speedup?
variants: Quantizing the model halves latency. How do you check what it costs in accuracy, and for which users?
You could drop the 20 slowest features. How would you decide which ones are worth their cost?

prodml-008.base: Which one can you detect without labels?
variants: You have no labels for the past three months. Which kind of drift can you still monitor, and how?
Customer demographics look unchanged, but buying behavior has shifted after a competitor's launch. Which kind of drift is this, and can you see it without labels?

prodml-008.base: Can a model be hurt by data drift without any concept drift?
variants: More applicants now come from a region your model saw little of in training. Can that hurt performance even if the region's behavior is the same?
Why can a shift in inputs hurt the model even when the underlying relationship hasn't changed?

prodml-008.base: What do you do differently when you see each?
variants: You confirm concept drift. Is retraining on more of the same history the right fix?
You confirm the inputs shifted but the relationship held. What actions make sense?

prodml-009.base: How would you measure the damage?
variants: How would you estimate how well the model would do on applicants it rejected?
How could a small random holdout of approvals help you measure the bias in your training data?

prodml-009.base: What would you change in how the data is collected?
variants: The business won't approve risky applicants at random. What other ways do you have to learn about rejected applicants?
What is reject inference, and why is it hard to get right?

prodml-009.base: What risk does this create in production over time?
variants: After several retraining cycles, the model approves an ever-narrower group. Why does that happen?
How would you monitor for a feedback loop like this before it does damage?

prodml-010.base: What signals would trigger a retrain?
variants: Which monitoring signals would justify an unscheduled retrain?
Labels for this model arrive 90 days late. How does that affect when you can retrain?

prodml-010.base: How do you make sure a retrained model is actually better?
variants: The retrained model scores better on a random test split. Why isn't that enough?
How would you run a champion-challenger comparison before switching models?

prodml-010.base: What can go wrong with retraining too often?
variants: Your model retrains every night, and its predictions for the same customer swing from day to day. What's the problem, and how do you fix it?
When does continuous retraining make a model chase noise rather than signal?

prodml-011.base: How do you choose the bins?
variants: Your PSI changes a lot when you switch from 10 bins to 20. Which do you trust?
How would you bin a feature that's mostly zeros with a long tail?

prodml-011.base: What does a high PSI tell you, and what doesn't it?
variants: A feature has PSI 0.4, but the model's accuracy hasn't moved. What does that tell you?
PSI on the model's score is high. What does that mean, and what doesn't it mean?

prodml-011.base: What would you use for a large set of features?
variants: You monitor 300 features. Is computing PSI on each one and alerting above 0.25 a good idea?
What drift measures would you use for categorical features with thousands of values?

prodml-012.base: What problems does it solve, and what does it cost?
variants: Your team has three models and each computes its own features. What would a feature store fix, and what new work would it create?
What does it cost to run a feature store well, beyond the software itself?

prodml-012.base: When would you say not yet?
variants: A startup with one model in production wants a feature store. Would you build one? What would you do instead?
What signs would tell you a team has outgrown simple feature pipelines?

prodml-012.base: How does it relate to training-serving skew?
variants: How does a shared feature definition for training and serving reduce training-serving skew?
Can a feature store still leave you with skew? How?

prodml-013.base: What do you check before touching the model?
variants: An upstream team deployed a change to transaction logging two days ago. How do you check whether it explains the drop?
What data checks would you run in the first hour, before looking at the model at all?

prodml-013.base: How do you tell a real change in fraud patterns from a data issue?
variants: The drop is concentrated in one merchant category and one country. Is that more likely fraud or a data problem? How do you confirm?
What evidence would convince you fraudsters changed tactics rather than your data changing?

prodml-013.base: What do you tell stakeholders in the first few hours?
variants: The head of risk asks whether to switch the model off. What do you tell them with only partial information?
How would you word a first status update when you don't yet know the cause?

prodml-014.base: Which signals are standard for every model, and which are model-specific?
variants: Which checks would every model get by default, and what would teams add themselves?
How do you give 10 teams consistent monitoring without forcing them all onto the same metrics?

prodml-014.base: How do you decide who gets paged?
variants: A model that sets prices drifts at 2 a.m. Who gets paged, and who gets an email?
How do you define severity levels for model alerts?

prodml-014.base: How do you know your alerts are any good?
variants: How would you measure whether your alerts are useful?
A team never acts on its alerts. What does that tell you, and what do you change?

prodml-015.base: What could a 30% override rate mean?
variants: Overrides are concentrated among two reviewers and one product type. What does that suggest?
Is a 30% override rate a sign the model is bad? What else could explain it?

prodml-015.base: How could the overrides become training data, and what are the risks?
variants: You want to retrain on reviewer decisions. What could go wrong with treating them as ground truth?
How would you check whether overrides were correct before using them as labels?

prodml-015.base: What if reviewers stop looking and just accept the model?
variants: Override rates drop to 2% after a few months. Good news, or a warning sign?
How would you check that reviewers are still exercising judgment?
